freshness.title: Freshness by dataset
freshness.subtitle: Measured now, against each dataset's service level (derived from API-Football's real update cadence).

sla.fixtures: Every current season's fixture list read in the last 14 h (sync every 6 h; the provider updates every 15 s).
sla.results: A match 3 h past kick-off carries a final status; if we re-read it and the provider still says NS, that is its lag.
sla.live: A match in play was read in the last 3 minutes (follower every 60 s).
sla.standings: The table was read after the season's last match ended (the provider updates hourly); asked after and unchanged = its lag.
sla.injuries: A season playing in the next 48 h had its list read in the last 6 h (the provider updates every 4 h).
sla.lineups: A match played in the last 7 days has its line-ups.
sla.match_detail: A match played in the last 7 days had its events and statistics read after it ended.
sla.odds_prematch: A match in the next 72 h was priced at the most recent capture window it reached (T-72/48/24/12/6/3 h, aligned on the provider's 3-hourly update).
sla.elo: Every match finished in the last 30 days carries a rating once the next 6-hourly recompute has run; a match without a stored score cannot be rated.
sla.teams: Identity (country, venue, crest) read in the last 120 days.
sla.players: The profile of everyone in a line-up in the last 365 days was read in the last 45 days (monthly sweep of /players/profiles).
sla.coaches: A profile has been read for every coach in a line-up in the last 365 days.
sla.coverage: The provider's coverage flags for each current season read in the last 8 days.
sla.squads: Every team of a current season had its squad read in the last 8 days (weekly round of /players/squads).

register.title: The 14 datasets
register.subtitle: Class, whether a model may use it, and the evidence. Dataset version for models: {version} ({status}). Measured {when}.
register.legend: FRESH: current. STALE: the provider has newer data and asking was our job. INCOMPLETE: 5% or more never read. INVALID: an open critical or high finding at PrediGol's fault. UNKNOWN: nothing to measure now. What the provider does not have never counts against us. A model may only use a FRESH dataset inside a MODEL_READY data version.
